prompt: What does 'volatile' do on a field?
choices: Makes reads/writes atomic for all types
Ensures all threads see the most up-to-date value by reading/writing directly to main memory
Prevents the field from being garbage collected
Makes the field thread-local (each thread has its own copy)
explanation: volatile guarantees visibility: a write by one thread is immediately visible to all others. It does NOT guarantee atomicity for compound operations like i++ (read-modify-write). For atomicity, use AtomicInteger or synchronized. Use volatile for simple flags like 'boolean running = true;'.
